stem:
Consider the following statement :
1. Natural gas occurs in the Gondwana belts.
2. Mica occurs in abundance in Kodarma.
3. Dharwars are famous for petroleum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Petroleum and natural gas are found in the sedimentary rocks of the tertiary plate. Gondwana belts belong to the upper Palaeozoic and Mesozoic periods and the Dharwar rocks belong to the late Archean period. Both these rocks are of a much older period and consist mostly of metamorphosed rocks and thus are very poor in petroleum and natural gases. Hence, both statements 1 and 3 are incorrect. Kodarma lies in Jharkhand and is quite famous for its mica. That is why it is called as the 'Mica City of India'. Thus, only statement 2 is correct and the right answer is option (b).

stem: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Natural gas is found in Dharwar rock formation.

options.label: c
options.text: Cuddapah series is famous for diamonds.

options.label: d
options.text: Petroleum reserves are found in Aravalli hills.

expl: Natural gas is found in sedimentary basins, generally in the areas of marine sediments. Hence statement (a) is incorrect. Significantly, Kodarma district of Jharkhand state has been famous worldwide for mica mining, especially for ruby mica. The main reserve of mica is found under the forest of Wildlife Sanctuary of Kodarma. Cuddapah basin has been well known for- barytes, asbestos, copper, iron, lead, diamond, uranium etc. Petroleum is found in Krishna, Godavari, Cauvery basin, Assam, Gujarat and Rajasthan.

stem: Which among the following is connected with Metamorphic rock ?
expl: Metamorphic rocks are a result of a transformation of existing rock, in a process called metamorphism, which means "change in form". Metamorphic minerals are those that form only at the high temperatures and pressures associated with the process of metamorphism.

stem: Quartzite is metamorphosed from :
expl: Quartzite is a non-foliated metamorphic rock composed almost entirely of quartz. It forms when a quartz-rich sandstone is altered by the heat, pressure and chemical activity of metamorphism.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Balaghat, Jabalpur, Jhabua and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh are an important region for manganese-ore production in India. In Balaghat, the main areas of mining are Katgaria, Langur, Verwali, Netra, Torodi, Batjari, Salwa and Chikpara. Diamond is found in the Majhgawan area in Panna district of Madhya Pradesh. The reserve of diamond in this area is about one million carats. So both the statements (1) and (2) are not correct. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
expl: The heavy mineral sand deposits in Kerala contain an assemblage of Ilmenite, Rutile, Leucoxene, Monazite, Zircon and Sillimanite. The state possesses one of the world class deposits of mineral sand in the coastal tracts between Neendakara and Kayamkulam. Hence (b) is the correct answer.

stem: Ilmenite and rutile, abundantly available in certain coastal tracts of India, are rich sources of which one of the following?
expl: India has abundant heavy mineral resources, most of which are found along the country's coast and also in inland plac-ers. The seven minerals that constitute heavy mineral sands include rutile, zircon, sillimanite, garnet, ilmenite, monazite and leucoxene (brown ilmenite). The main sources of titanium are rutile and ilmenite.

stem: The Central Government has announced the opening of first lithium mine of India in which of the following districts of Chhattisgarh?
expl: Lithium reserves by the Geological Survey of India (GSI). The Central Government decided to open the first lithium mine in the Katghora region of Korba district, Chhattisgarh in August 2024. This announcement was made during the sixth Governing Body meeting of the National Mineral Exploration Trust in New Delhi. The GSI reported lithium concentrations ranging from 10 to 2,000 parts per million (PPM) over an area of approximately 250 hectares, with the possibility of even higher concentration.
